card.title: New Ticket card — three defaults
card.message: Question 1 of 3: Default priority on your New Ticket card? Question 2 of 3: Where should a new ticket go by default? Question 3 of 3: Should your own tickets skip the ratio gate?

options.label: P2 (Recommended)
options.description: Pro: a routine ticket lands mid-board and P0 stays deliberate. Con: an urgent ticket needs one extra click.

options.label: P0
options.description: Pro: fastest when filing something urgent. Con: every quick note lands above all live work unless you lower it.

options.label: P5
options.description: Pro: matches the store's default. Con: your tickets start at the bottom of the board.

questions.question: Default priority on your New Ticket card?

options.label: Live board (Recommended)
options.description: Pro: no approval wait, which is the point of the card. Con: a half-formed idea is on the board right away.

options.label: Holding area
options.description: Pro: park ideas and admit them later. Con: brings back the wait, unless you switch it each time.

questions.question: Where should a new ticket go by default?

options.label: Yes, logged (Recommended)
options.description: Pro: your P1 to P5 tickets can't be refused for throughput; every use is logged like the P0 exemption. Con: the board can grow faster than work closes.

options.label: No
options.description: Pro: one throughput rule for everyone. Con: while the gate enforces, your P1 to P5 tickets can come back refused.

questions.question: Should your own tickets skip the ratio gate?
